subject: 🏃 Friday — Short Easy Run + Strides (Wk 7, 2 Days to Presidio)
html:
Tomorrow: ~2–2.5 miles very easy + 4–6 strides — a pre-race primer, nothing more. You elected to swap out the loaded Stability & Power session, and that was the right call: the knee flagged 2/5 off Wednesday’s squats and you want it fresh for Sunday. This run primes the neuromuscular system without adding fatigue.

Pre-run activation (5 min): Quadruped hip CARs (3 each direction) → banded lateral walks (10 each) → glute bridges (10 reps, 2-sec hold) → PT-prescribed quadruped banded hip IR (5–10 reps each side).

The run:

  • 2–2.5 miles very easy — HR ≤140 (low Z2, no pushing). Door route is fine; let pace float with the hills. This should feel like a jog, not a run.
  • Then 4–6 × ~20-sec strides on the flattest stretch you can find near home. Relaxed build to ~mile/5K effort — NOT sprints. Full walk-back recovery between each. These are about turnover and snap, not speed. Stop strides immediately at any knee signal.

Focus cue: Light feet, quick cadence on the strides. Think about the Presidio start — relaxed, controlled, and sharp. If anything feels off in the legs or the knee, cut the strides short. You’re 48 hours from the pivot test; nothing you do tomorrow builds fitness, but something aggressive could steal freshness.

Where you are: Week 7 of 12, Phase 2. Presidio HM is Sunday morning — the gated pivot test (sub-1:37:30 / HR <170 final 3 mi / zero knee comp). The taper week has been clean: Tuesday’s 3×1600m was dead-even at 7:09–7:13/mi and HR 155–158, Thursday’s progression was well-governed (knee back to 1/5 after the squat-driven 2), and the engine looks sharp. Saturday is full rest. You’re arriving at the start line in good shape.

Tonight: Lay out your run kit for a short, easy morning. Hydrate well. Review the RACE_PLAN_PRESIDIO.md mile-by-mile strategy before bed if you haven’t already — internalize the pacing plan now so Sunday morning is automatic. Bed by 10.
